name: Michael Nash
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Mo Yuezhang' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Michael Nash' was chosen as a dignified, professional name fitting a senior guild official; verified by matching scenes (greeting Zane personally, clapping for servants, Eps 427-428 vs Chs 414-415).
description: Michael Nash is the branch leader of the World Merchants' Guild (source: World Business Alliance) in the Cloudhaven/Oracle City region. A long-lived, powerful and courteous authority figure, he personally welcomes Zane as a guest of honor, evaluates his rune work, and later observes Zane's magic-array feats through a Scrying Slate with keen interest.

name: Razor
reason: The source monster species 'Blade Bug' (also rendered 'Saber Insect') was renamed 'Razor' to keep the sharp-edged imagery in a punchier Western register; episodes consistently speak of the 'Razor swarm'.
description: The Razors are swarm insects hunted by the imperial army out of Dragon's Keep during Zane's early soldier arc (Eps 60-82). They attack in overwhelming numbers, and defeating a Razor swarm leader earns an additional merit Point; Zane joins the hunts to accumulate Points for entry into Infernal Peak.

name: Inner World
reason: The source's English term 'Inner World' was kept unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: The Inner World is a personal internal dimension that warriors open upon reaching the Spirit Supreme Realm: their Vitality liquefies into a spiritual sea stored inside it. Zane's Inner World is unusual — it holds no Vitality but instead houses the World Tree sapling, which draws in threads of Chaos Energy for him.

name: Ogres'
reason: Possessive fragment: 'Ogres'' is simply the possessive form of the Ogre race (source: Demon Race/Demon Clan), whose mentions are covered by the 'Ogre' race entity; capitalized occurrences are all 'Ogres' Sacred Land', covered by that entity.

name: Ogres' Sacred Land
issues: Source speaks of the Demon Clan owning TWO Sacred Lands ('Twin Devil Holy Lands'); the episodes consolidate this into a single 'Ogres' Sacred Land'.
reason: The source faction 'Twin Devil Holy Land' (the Demon Clan's Holy Land on the Sea God Continent) was localized as 'Ogres' Sacred Land', matching the show's renaming of the Demon Race to Ogres.
description: The Ogres' Sacred Land is the ruling Holy Land of the Ogre race on the war-torn continent of the Tower of Sin arc, powerful enough that the Violet Heart Sanctuary declaring war on it is likened to a child squaring up to an armed soldier. It receives intelligence from the Twilight Group, and within two hundred years is ultimately suppressed by the Violet Heart Sanctuary under its new leader (Ep 920).

name: Dark Nether Death Light
reason: The source term 'Mysterious Underworld Death Ray' (Xuan Ming Death Ray) was renamed 'Dark Nether Death Light' for a smoother Western fantasy register, consistent with 'Dark Nether Cave' for the source's Mysterious Underworld Cave.
description: The Dark Nether Death Light is a lethal, radiation-like force that floods the Dark Nether Cave year-round, able to melt any living thing into a puddle no matter how powerful. It pours from a mysterious red dot deep in the cave and intensifies the closer one gets; expeditions can only enter when it periodically weakens (Eps 580-680).

name: Black Fire
reason: The source's 'black flame' of the mysterious furnace in Luo Zheng's mind was localized as 'Black Fire', a near-literal rendering kept as a proper noun.
description: The Black Fire is the enigmatic flame inside the mysterious Furnace in Zane's mindscape. It first manifested by refining the Hellfire Blade into pure Celestial Essence, forges weapons for Zane, and behaves like a living thing — consuming celestial essence restores its strength and can awaken the Dragon Scales tied to the dragon in his mind.

name: Rhys Bolton
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhang Wuxian' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Rhys' with surname 'Bolton' was chosen for Zane's streetwise, well-informed sect friend; the match is supported by Zhang Wuxian's role explaining the sect's points/punishment system (Ch 44) mirroring Rhys Bolton's 'Two Paths to Prison' exposition (Eps 52-53) and his presence through the Eps 194-208 arc.
description: Rhys Bolton is one of Zane's closest allies in the sect (Eps 52-208), a cheerful, enterprising disciple of humble origins with no noteworthy connections. He knows the sect's rules and rumor mill inside out, travels with Zane and Dustin, and throws himself enthusiastically into their ventures.

name: Psyche Spike
reason: The source technique 'Frightening Spirit Thorn' (also rendered 'Frightening Divine Thorn') was renamed 'Psyche Spike' — a compact Western name that preserves the soul-attack imagery.
description: The Psyche Spike is Zane's signature soul-attack technique, a Heaven-class esoteric art manifesting as a pale-yellow thorn launched from the forehead. It disrupts an opponent's concentration — even a split-second blackout can decide a fight — and it places no demands on cultivation realm, only on the strength of the user's soul. Zane relies on it from his earliest duels through the later arcs (Eps 52-829).

name: Saint Augustus
reason: The character's Daoist name 'Zhenren Tianqiong' was fully localized: the title 'Zhenren' (Perfected Person) became 'Saint' and the name was replaced with 'Augustus', a weighty Latin name fitting a stern sect elder; confirmed by the matching judgment scene against Zane over Zhuge Feng's death (Eps 174-176 vs Chs 157-161).
description: Saint Augustus is a powerful, imperious elder of the sect who passes harsh judgment on Zane after the killing of a noble scion, threatening that no one will be able to protect him. Notorious for his unwavering confidence, he is visibly checked when Isla's royal authority intervenes and demands an explanation for his precipitous judgment (Eps 174-279).

name: Harrison
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xu Han' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Harrison'; confirmed by the matching scene in which Zane steadies him with Vitality at a critical moment and Harrison bows in thanks (Ep 215 vs Chs 201-204).
description: Harrison is the Eldest Senior Brother of a weapon-crafting academy (source: Seventeenth Courtyard of Dipping Fire Peak) whom Zane saves from a disastrous furnace mishap by pouring steady Vitality into him (Ep 215). Grateful, he offers Zane his help and the use of his forge, treating him with deep respect.

name: Phoenix
reason: The source's 'Phoenix' (Fire Phoenix / Phoenix Clan) was kept unchanged as a well-known mythical creature name in the Western register.
description: The Phoenix is a legendary fire-aligned race in the world of the show, a symbol of immortality whose true flames — the Flames of Rebirth — can burn even masters of third-layer Fire Law to nothing (Eps 818-821). Descendants of the Phoenix Race appear among the cast, and the name also figures in related entities such as the Heavenly Phoenix Horses.

name: Scorpiomane
reason: The source beast 'Fire Scorpion' (whose Crystal Core appears in Chs 55-82) was renamed 'Scorpiomane', an invented portmanteau evoking a scorpion-lion hybrid for the Western fantasy bestiary.
description: The Scorpiomane is a fearsome apex-predator beast Zane encounters in a cavern during the Razor-hunt arc (Eps 69-97), where it battles the Razorwing Queen in a clash of titans before being fatally wounded. Its monster core is so valuable that the seven Great Houses would kill to obtain one.

name: Enchanted Barrier Tower
reason: The source trial tower rendered 'Thought Sealed Tower' / 'Thought Boundary Tower' (Chs ~1055-1090) was renamed 'Enchanted Barrier Tower' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: The Enchanted Barrier Tower is a deadly trial site in the Thirteen Palaces arc (Eps 1076-1244), filled with an endless Law Storm that separates even companions like Zane and Layla. Surviving its test is a mark of extraordinary strength — observers remark it would be a shame for a warrior as incredible as Zane to die inside it.

name: Heavenly Phoenix Horse
reason: The source mount 'Heavenly Luan Horse' was localized as 'Heavenly Phoenix Horse', substituting the obscure 'luan' (a Chinese phoenix-like bird) with the familiar 'Phoenix'.
description: The Heavenly Phoenix Horse is a legendary, priceless mount and the ultimate status symbol in the Upper World arc (Eps 1041-1124). Exceptionally fast and ridden by figures such as Freya, even this legendary beast has an instinctual fear of truly terrifying powers.

name: Endless Abyss
reason: The source trial ground 'Samsara Abyss' (also 'Abyss of Samsara') was renamed 'Endless Abyss', trading the Buddhist term for a simpler Western fantasy name.
description: The Endless Abyss is an ancient trial ground established eons ago by the Supreme Lord (source: an ancient Empyrean), who scattered its keys and clues across the entire universe (Eps 1138-1172). It is structured as five concentric laps or rings of escalating danger — the fourth is the domain of a Demon Night Saint Lord — and dispenses rewards to those who penetrate deeper, with Lavender guiding Zane through its early prizes.

name: Eternal Scribe
reason: The source character's title-name 'Book Immortal' (Immortal of Books) was localized as 'Eternal Scribe', preserving the bookish immortal concept in a Western idiom; confirmed by the matching scene of him recommending books and snorting 'Hmph!' at a skeptical girl (Eps 983-985 vs Chs 960-969).
description: The Eternal Scribe is the proud, bookish custodian of a vast library encountered in Eps 983-995 (source: the Book Immortal of the Immortal Mansion arc). Prickly when his collection is doubted — snorting at Cora's claim that nothing there would interest her — he warms to worthy visitors, guiding Zane through the stacks and approving his work with a quiet nod.

name: Legacy House
reason: The source's privileged 'landowning clans' / great aristocratic families were localized as 'Legacy Houses' — the show's confirmed canonical term (NOT 'Legacy Families') — conveying inherited noble privilege in a Western register.
description: Legacy Houses are the hereditary noble houses of the early arcs (Eps 28-126), such as House Warrick, whose scions enjoy sweeping privileges: separate application lines, first turns at trials, and vastly higher pass rates in The Gauntlet (170 of 200 Legacy scions passing versus 200 of 1,000 commoners). Their wealth makes point penalties trivial for their disciples, and defying them as a lone commoner, as Zane does, is considered reckless.

name: Jon
issues: Merged entity: the dossier folds 'Jones' (7 mentions, Eps 1226-1273+) into 'Jon', but 'Jones' there is the surname of Zane's alias 'Zane Jones', not this character. Jon the retainer only appears in Eps 72-79 and 185.
reason: 'Jon' is a plain US-origin name assigned to a minor retainer character in the Dragon's Keep arc; no distinct source counterpart is identifiable in the evidence, so he appears to be adaptation connective tissue.
description: Jon is Leo Brandt's wiry, anxious retainer, who has served the Brandt family since boyhood (Eps 72-79). A cautious veteran, he persistently warns Leo against provoking the Sterling family and physically steps between Randall and his targets, insisting that beating on a kid will not make anyone look good.

name: Immovable Guardian
reason: The source's Buddhist deity 'Acalanatha' (the Immovable Wisdom King) was localized as 'The Immovable Guardian', keeping the 'immovable' epithet while removing the specifically Buddhist name.
description: The Immovable Guardian is a legendary being whose terrifying spectral shadow and crushing palm can be summoned by Patrick (source: Pei Tianyao), who is revealed to be the Guardian's reincarnation (Eps 306-312). Disciples recognize the summoned 'Immovable Guardian's Palm' on sight, and it is powerful enough to block Finn's Sword of Celestial Judgment infused with Extreme Thunder Sword Intent.

name: Doug
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhuo Feiyi' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Doug Drew'; confirmed by the matching banquet duel scene — a refined man in white with coarse words who shapes Vitality into bird-like claws and wings for a self-created movement technique (Eps 339-340 vs Ch 327).
description: Doug Drew is a minor antagonist at Prince Ray's banquet (Eps 339-341), dressed head to toe in white and looking refined and handsome while speaking with startling coarseness. Recently broken through to the Soul Realm, he famously created his own bird-mimicking movement technique — shaping Vitality into claws and wings for extreme speed — but is nonetheless defeated easily by Zane.

name: Enchanted Lamp
reason: The source quest item 'Immortal Tomb Spirit Lamp' (Spirit Lamp) was renamed 'Enchanted Lamp', with the associated Immortal Tomb localized as the Celestial Tomb of Vesper.
description: The Enchanted Lamps are nine legendary quest items tied to the Celestial Tomb of Vesper: lighting all nine opens the tomb, and lighting one is itself a lifelong dream for many warriors (Eps 400-721). Most fall into the hands of major Heartlands factions; Tia and Kieran each possess one, and lighting a lamp inside the tomb means nothing within stays secret.

name: Original Laws
reason: The source term 'Source Laws' was localized as 'Original Laws', a near-synonymous rendering kept consistent across the adaptation.
description: The Original Laws are the nine fundamental forces underlying the world's power system — Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth, Wind, Electricity and two unnamed others — each divided into ten layers (per the master sheet, Eps 460-500). Mastering them defines high-level combat: warriors meditate on them for power, elite attacks are formed from their strongest energies, and Zane mastered all nine in the upper world (Eps 437-1289).

name: Thunder Law
reason: The source term 'Law of Thunder' (also 'Thunder Laws') was localized as 'Thunder Law', matching the show's '<Element> Law' naming convention for the Original Laws.
description: The Thunder Law is one of the Original Laws, a layered lightning principle whose early levels in the source are named Destruction, Purification and Heavenly Tribulation. Zane progresses through its layers across the saga (Eps 488-1208), from recognizing rivals who had barely scratched its first layer to seeking sacred World Tree shoots that could unlock its sixth level.

name: Jeffrey
issues: Distinct from the MasterLS entry 'Jeff' (Ep 247, ranked 99th in Skyreach Sect Rankings) — that is a different minor character; this Jeffrey appears only in Eps 1273-1315.
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Jin Hai' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Jeffrey'; confirmed by the matching line — 'It's the Law of Darkness,' Jin Hai said coldly (Ch ~1256) vs 'It's the power of the Dark Law,' Jeffrey said grimly (Ep 1275).
description: Jeffrey is a capable warrior in Zane's party during the Illusion Battlefield arc (Eps 1273-1315), fighting alongside Janet and the others against Demon Race cultivators. Grim and knowledgeable, he is the one who identifies the enemy's Dark Law at work, and in the source he wields both a hook and the Buddha Sun Blade.

name: Jarrod
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhao Fenqin' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Jarrod'; confirmed by the matching dialogue — 'Fen Qin, isn't there a Book of Heaven Rank at the top of the tower?' (source) vs Fabian asking Jarrod about the Book of Celestial Rank (Ep 601).
description: Jarrod is one of the four human seat holders in the Tower of Sin arc (Eps 597-953), a knowledgeable companion of Malcolm, Fabian and Olivia who knows the tower's lore, including the Book of Celestial Rank at its top. Level-headed and pragmatic, he soberly calls the fight over when two War Sages enter the field, and his counsel usually proves sound.
